description:
We are a team of enthusiastic tech enthusiasts passionate about AI/ML, space technology, data science, and innovative problem-solving. 

We welcome collaborative individuals who are excited to contribute, experiment, and build together. We are particularly looking for members with skills in AI/ML, Python, geospatial analysis (GIS), satellite data processing, remote sensing, frontend development, and UI/UX design.
summary:
TerraTwin is an AI-powered planetary exploration platform designed to discover and analyze Earth locations that resemble the geological and terrain characteristics of regions on the Moon and Mars.

The platform allows users to explore extraterrestrial landscapes, identify potential Earth-based analogues, and compare planetary and terrestrial environments through interactive visualizations and scientific similarity analysis. It brings together planetary exploration, geospatial data, and AI-assisted research to make the discovery of terrestrial analogues more accessible and insightful.

TerraTwin addresses the challenge by providing a practical way to identify Earth environments that can help researchers study extraterrestrial terrain, understand geological formations, and explore potential locations for testing planetary exploration technologies. By connecting Earth-based landscapes with lunar and Martian environments, TerraTwin aims to bridge the gap between planetary science and real-world exploration, supporting research, education, and future space missions.
details:
TerraTwin is an AI-powered Planetary Analog Discovery Platform that helps identify Earth locations with terrain and geological characteristics similar to selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

How it works: Users can interact with detailed 3D Moon and Mars globes, select specific coordinates, and define an exploration radius. TerraTwin then analyzes potential Earth analogues from a database containing over 600 candidate locations across seven continents. Its scientific comparison engine evaluates 11 physical and geological parameters, including slope, terrain ruggedness, elevation, surface albedo, thermal properties, rock coverage, and lithology. Using Z-score normalization, weighted distance calculations, and geological compatibility scoring, it ranks Earth locations according to their relative similarity to the selected extraterrestrial region.

Key capabilities and benefits: The platform features interactive 3D planetary exploration, global Earth analogue discovery, synchronized side-by-side planetary comparisons, scientific similarity radar charts, elevation profiles, and detailed physical parameter comparisons. Its AI Mission Research Assistant, powered by Groq's Llama 3.3 70B model, provides mission-oriented insights for rover mobility, robotic drilling, and scientific sensor calibration. Users can also generate downloadable PDF research reports containing comparison metrics, mission suitability assessments, environmental limitations, and scientific references.

Technology and tools: The frontend uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and CesiumJS. The backend is developed using Python 3.13 and FastAPI, with NumPy, SciPy, Scikit-learn, Pydantic, and SQLite supporting scientific computation, spatial indexing, and data management. Groq provides LLM integration, while ReportLab and Pillow handle PDF generation. The platform incorporates scientific datasets from NASA LRO (LOLA, LROC, Diviner), NASA MGS MOLA, NASA THEMIS, NASA MODIS, USGS SRTM, the Global Lithological Map (GLiM), and ECMWF ERA5-Land.

Creativity and innovation: TerraTwin combines planetary science, geospatial computing, mathematical similarity modelling, interactive 3D visualization, and AI-assisted mission research into one integrated platform. Instead of relying on visual resemblance alone, it uses multiple measurable scientific parameters to produce explainable comparisons and ranked candidate locations.

Intended impact and considerations: TerraTwin aims to make planetary analogue research more accessible, help researchers identify promising terrestrial testing environments, and support preliminary exploration and mission-planning studies. The team considered geological compatibility, terrain morphology, thermal characteristics, vegetation differences, data availability, computational efficiency, and the physical differences between Earth and extraterrestrial environments. Importantly, TerraTwin treats similarity as a comparative research indicator rather than proof that two environments are physically identical. Factors such as gravity, atmospheric pressure, radiation, and the absence of a lunar or Martian atmosphere must also be considered before applying Earth-based findings to actual space missions.
